title: Raft leader election (one term, staggered election timers)
source: Ongaro and Ousterhout, "In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm" (USENIX ATC 2014), Section 5.2 and Figure 2, election only: logs are empty and log replication is left out (file header, lines 3-8). Election Safety is the property of Figure 3 of that paper. The timing (stagger unit delta, L = 0, U = 1, sd = (N - 1) * delta) is our own; the Raft paper states no such rule.
property: Election Safety, at most one leader per term: every node remembers the first (term, leader) it sees and asserts that its own election and every later AppendEntries of the same term name the same leader (record_leader, lines 193-201).
citable_note: The two modes do not run the same program: the timed mode has a staggered sleep, a zero-wait peek receive and a deterministic candidacy rule where the baseline has one nondeterministic choice (lines 351-353, 358-374, 382-393), so the two counts measure two different models. The 2026-09-18 audit verdict (not citable) holds on the current source; in addition --rounds has no effect (unconditional return at line 442) and the timed side explores 3.3 times more than the baseline.
config_timed: build_config, lines 453-470: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_timed(0, 1, sd).with_progress_report(100_000).with_verbose(0), with sd = (N - 1) * delta computed at line 464 (N = 3, delta = 2: sd = 4). L = 0 and U = 1 are fixed in the source, there is no flag for them. Tool defaults for the rest (lib.rs, ConfigBuilder::new, lines 347-383): consistency model FIFO, scheduling policy LTR, keep-going off, sequential (the binary has no parallel option). Every send may be dropped, without a budget. The Init handoff is send_msg_timed(.., 0, 0) (line 494). Receives: blocking (lines 340 and 431) and the peek with wait 0 (line 362).
config_baseline: build_config, lines 449-452: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(100_000).with_verbose(0): FIFO, LTR, keep-going off, sequential; every send may be dropped, without a budget. No clock. delta is not used in this mode (the local binary prints the same counts for --delta 2 and --delta 7).
program_differs_between_modes: yes: three mode-dependent blocks in the protocol code of the node function, which takes the mode as a parameter (line 333, passed at line 482). (1) Lines 351-353: if mode == Mode::Timed, sleep((me + 1) * delta), the staggered election timer, timed only. (2) Lines 358-374: the peek; the baseline sets saw_message_in_peek = false without receiving, the timed mode does recv_msg_timed(WaitTime::Finite(0)), handles the message and may send a reply (line 367). (3) Lines 382-393: the decision to stand for election; baseline: not Leader, current_term < round, and traceforge::nondet(); timed: deterministic (still Follower, has not voted, nothing read in the peek).
failing_tasks: Node threads only: traceforge::assert at line 197 (record_leader), reached from become_leader (line 217) and from the AppendEntries handler (line 294). Under keep-going the line would read task-N; this binary has no keep-going option, so a violation would stop the run at the first certified violation with exit code 101. The main thread asserts nothing. No violation occurred in any run.

value of --rounds, meant as the highest term; it has no effect, the node function returns at the end of the first round (line 442)

regimes.name: staggered election timers
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=4, delta=2 (the nodes sleep 2, 4 and 6 ticks before their election step; timed side only)
regimes.rule: No timing boundary: Election Safety holds with and without the clock in the single term that is run. Control for the verdict only (the two sides must agree on 0 violations). The two sides run different programs, so their execution counts are not a measure of what the clock removes.

glossary.meaning: Raft's election epoch; only term 1 is ever run, whatever --rounds says
a candidate asks every peer for its vote; a node grants at most one vote per term
sent by a node to every peer once it has a majority of votes; logs are empty, so it carries only (term, leader)
at most one leader per term, checked locally by every node on its own election and on every heartbeat it receives

timed side only: node i sleeps (i + 1) * delta ticks, so the election timers fire one after the other. It models the common case of spread-out timers; it is a different scenario from the baseline, not the same program with fewer interleavings.
timed side only: one receive with wait 0 after the sleep, to see whether a message of an earlier candidate is already there; the node stands for election only if it read nothing
baseline only: each node decides with traceforge::nondet() whether its election timer fires, so every subset of the nodes may stand
a node waits forever on its blocking receive: no leader emerged (split vote) or the message it needs was lost. With every send lossy this is the large majority of the explored executions.
the cell is kept as a record of the v8 row; it must not be used as evidence for or against the timed checker

notes: Not citable. Audit of 2026-09-18 checked against the current source: it names line 351 plus two mode-dependent branches; they are at lines 351-353 (timed-only sleep), 358-374 (timed-only peek receive) and 382-393 (nondeterministic choice in the baseline, deterministic rule in timed mode). The standing rule (memory note three_pc_delta_commit_feasibility) forbids mode-conditional sleeps in a benchmark that compares the two modes; the note feedback_raft_temporal_framing adds that the stagger models a different scenario, so the baseline and the timed mode explore different state spaces.

--rounds is a no-op (memory note project_v8_campaign): confirmed. The for loop over rounds ends in an unconditional return at line 442, so only round 1 runs. Checked on the local binary: --rounds 1 and --rounds 3 print the same counts in both modes. The file header (lines 1, 10-24, 113, 117-120) still describes a multi-term, R-bounded model; that text is out of date.
The summary line prints only nodes and R (line 502): delta, L, U and sd do not appear in it. They are resolved from the source: L = 0 and U = 1 at line 466, sd = (N - 1) * delta = 4 at line 464.

v8 numbers: the row legacy-019 of results_v8.csv (timed, blocked=25304) was measured under the W = 0 rule that was withdrawn on 2026-09-30 and must be ignored; the rerun legacy-019-A in results_v8_w0A.csv has blocked=38503, which is what v9 measures. The baseline counts are the same in v8 and v9.
The timed side explores more than the baseline (41215 against 12596 explored, 9.3 s against 0.6 s). Complete executions: 2712 timed, 2232 baseline.
violation_counter is null and counters is empty: the summary line has no counter. The violating-execution count 0 comes from the exit code.

kind: the binary has no keep-going option (ConfigBuilder default, lib.rs line 353), so the cell is first-violation by the rule of FORMAT.md; the runs exit with code 0, which means that no violation exists and the whole space was explored.

Regime suffix: the first draft used S-safe. Changed to S-ctrl: there is no timing boundary and both sides report 0 violations, so the definition of -safe does not apply. Field family: the first draft had "raft"; set to "legacy", the family id of plan_v9.csv. The file name raft.json is kept as asked.
The source comment at lines 454-463 explains sd: with sd = 0 a late peek would find nothing and no leader would ever be elected, so sd is tied to delta by the source, not chosen freely.
